editorial:
You meet Earl Brooks, a respected businessman who seems to have it all: a loving family, a successful company, and a clean reputation. But he hides a dark secret. He is a serial killer, and his alter ego Marshall constantly pushes him to keep killing. When a witness catches him on camera, Brooks is forced into a dangerous game of blackmail and murder that threatens to destroy everything he has built.

Kevin Costner and William Hurt are fantastic together, and their back-and-forth gives the movie real energy. The pacing stays tense, and the plot has some clever twists. On the downside, a few side stories slow things down, and some characters feel underused. Still, if you enjoy psychological thrillers with strong acting, this one is worth your time. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or pick up the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Brooks kills the blackmailer and frames him for the murders, while his daughter reveals she has the same killer urges. Brooks plans to end her life to stop the cycle but cannot go through with it. The movie ends with Brooks waking from a nightmare where his daughter shoots him in bed, leaving you wondering if the darkness will continue in the family.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves psychological thrillers and crime dramas.
